description: Deterministic test fixtures for Pakanta iteration. Uses canonical S89-prefix IDs. Compatible with cross-iteration scenarios (same event_id appears in 0001, 0008, 0012, etc.)

customer_brief.story: We met on a bridge in Vigan during a backpacking trip. Two years later we're getting married on December 18, 2026. We want a song that captures that first moment — the surprise, the rain, the laughter.
Reception entrance song — we want something joyful and uptempo that gets everyone dancing.
customer_brief.reference_song: Kahit Maputi Na Ang Buhok Ko

pakanta_renders.approach_label: Take A · Lover-era bright pop · Taylor Swift inspired
pakanta_renders.suno_prompt_used: Bright indie pop, female lead vocal, warm and joyful. Major key, mid-tempo around 100 BPM. Clean electric guitar with light chorus pedal, layered acoustic guitar strums, soft synth pad, bouncy bass, full kit drums with crisp snare and tambourine, hand claps in the chorus. Vocal sits clear and forward in the mix, double-tracked with high harmony stack in the chorus hook. Polished radio-ready studio production. The story of meeting on a bridge in Vigan, the surprise of love. [End]
pakanta_renders.owner_notes: Take A explores the joyful Lover-era pop direction the brief hinted at.

pakanta_renders.approach_label: Take B · Folklore cottagecore acoustic · intimate storyteller
pakanta_renders.suno_prompt_used: Indie folk-pop, female lead vocal, intimate and whispery in verses, opening up in choruses. Major key, slow-mid tempo around 88 BPM. Fingerpicked acoustic guitar as the main texture, soft felt piano underneath, warm upright bass, brushed snare entering verse 2, light strings lifting the bridge. Storytelling vocal delivery, conversational, close-mic'd. Warm room reverb, vinyl-tape character, polished but unhurried. The feeling of a memory told quietly. The bridge moment in Vigan, the rain, the laughter. [End]
pakanta_renders.owner_notes: Take B explores the Folklore-feel direction as the contrasting approach. Sees the same brief as 'intimate memory' rather than 'joyful announcement'.

pakanta_renders.approach_label: Take A · Modern Filipino pop duet · OPM upbeat
pakanta_renders.suno_prompt_used: Modern OPM duet, male and female lead vocals trading lines then harmonizing in the chorus. Major key, upbeat around 112 BPM. Acoustic guitar foundation, light electric guitar lead, bouncy bass, full drums with tambourine, kundiman-flavored melodic phrasing in the bridge. Polished studio production. Reception entrance song energy.

pakanta_renders.approach_label: Take B · Classic kundiman with modern groove · acoustic-led
pakanta_renders.suno_prompt_used: Classic kundiman vibe with modern groove, male-female duet, female vocal lead in verses, male in pre-chorus, both in chorus. Major key, mid-tempo around 96 BPM. Fingerpicked nylon guitar foundation, soft bandurria fills, warm bass, light cajón percussion, strings swell into the bridge. Tagalog-friendly melodic phrasing. Romantic but danceable. Reception entrance song.

pakanta_renders.approach_label: Re-render 1 · Bigger chorus with horn section
pakanta_renders.suno_prompt_used: Same kundiman-modern groove as Take B, but expand the chorus with a brass horn section (trumpets + saxophone), more percussion in the chorus (kalutang + tambourine layered), and a key change up half a step for the final chorus. Keep the verse arrangement intimate.
pakanta_renders.owner_notes: Couple asked for 'bigger chorus, more celebratory' — added horns and key change.

pakanta_renders.suno_prompt_used: Same as re-render 1, but shorten the intro from 12 bars to 8 bars and start with light percussion instead of guitar alone. Punch into the first verse at 0:18 instead of 0:24.
pakanta_renders.owner_notes: Couple wanted shorter intro to hit the dance floor faster. Locked.
